一个并不AI原生的小团队，照常用微信和Notion，怎样接住一场千人大会前前后后几十轮修改？AIE上海我做的不只是后台，还有排议程、请嘉宾、宣传卖票和联系社区；这篇只复盘后台这一段：我人在西雅图，带着一个agent负责官网、议程和物料。从10月22日官网上线到大会结束，官网发布44次，73条修改需求上线66条，交付322张海报和大屏图。​
AI native不是每个环节都用上AI，而是保留大家最顺手的工作方式，找到其中最卡的那个限制，用AI把它撑大。 这次最卡的是交接：一条修改要在官网、PDF、海报、大屏之间传好几手。我们把这一整段交给一个人加一个agent走完。​
工具不换，只定一个“算数”的地方。 微信里商量，Notion里定稿

en.title: Behind the Scenes at AIE Shanghai: 50+ Speakers, a 1,000-Person Conference—How a Small Team Used AI to Seamlessly Absorb Dozens of Rounds of Changes
en.summary:
Behind the scenes at AIE Shanghai: 50+ speakers, a 1,000-person conference, and how a small team used AI invisibly to handle dozens of rounds of changes - Feishu Docs

Superlinear Academy

📌 This article is a repost; copyright belongs to the original author, and the full text is subject to the original link.

How does a team that isn't AI-native — still using WeChat and Notion as usual — absorb dozens of rounds of revisions before and after a 1,000-person conference? At AIE Shanghai I didn't just run the back office; I also built the agenda, invited speakers, handled promotion and ticket sales, and coordinated with communities. This piece recaps only the back-office part: I was in Seattle with a single agent responsible for the website, agenda and materials. From the site going live on October 22 to the end of the conference, the website shipped 44 releases, 66 of 73 change requests went live, and we delivered 322 posters and big-screen graphics.

Being AI native isn't about using AI at every step — it's about keeping the way everyone works most comfortably, finding the tightest bottleneck in it, and using AI to widen that bottleneck. This time the bottleneck was handoffs: a single change had to pass through several hands across the website, PDF, posters and the big screen. We handed that entire stretch to one person plus one agent to carry through.

Don't change tools, just designate one place that "counts." Discuss in WeChat, finalize in Notion

这个周末，老金刷红果，刷到一段抗战剧情，给我看得热泪盈眶。​
我做了这么久的游戏，看到这里，脑子里就冒出个念头：要是把这种感觉做进互动AVG，让人自己上手，会怎么样？​
我想做的AVG，就是那种跟着剧情玩的冒险游戏。故事演到你面前，你能做选择，也能动手帮上一把。​
这次GPT能用的能力里没有视频生成，所以游戏里用的全是图片。图是它自己生成的，配音模型是它自己找的，音效是它自己上网搜的，其他效果也都是它自己做的。​
《财经》引用QuestMobile的数据，2026年7、8月，红果App的月人均单日使用时长平均约151分钟，同期抖音是133.5分钟。​

就拿我自己来说，我在看短剧的时候，就喜欢打脸啊、反差呀这种剧情。​
情绪让人留下来，时间才有机会变成生意。​
说白了，先得让人想看下去，后面才有广告、付费解

en.title: With just two paragraphs, I got AI to build an AI game that moved me to tears.
en.summary:
With just two paragraphs, I got AI to build an AI game that brought tears to my eyes! - Feishu Docs

Jin Xiansen, Korean-Chinese · WeChat official account · Lao Jin Takes You Through AI · 2026-11-17 10:09

📌 This article is a repost; copyright belongs to the original author, and the full text is subject to the original link.

This weekend, Lao Jin was scrolling Hongguo when he came across a War of Resistance storyline that left him in tears.

Having made games for so long, a thought popped into my head as I watched: what if I put that feeling into an interactive AVG and let people play it themselves?

The AVG I wanted to make is that kind of story-driven adventure game. The story plays out in front of you, you can make choices, and you can also step in and lend a hand.

GPT's available capabilities this time didn't include video generation, so the game uses only images. It generated the images itself, found the voiceover model itself, searched the web for sound effects itself, and handled all the other effects itself too.

Caijing, citing QuestMobile data, reports that in July and August 2026, the Hongguo app averaged about 151 minutes of daily per-user time, versus 133.5 minutes for Douyin over the same period.

Spending that much time a day watching short dramas — what exactly are people watching?

en.title: From SDLC to ADLC: P&G's AI-Native Organization Experiment
en.summary:
AI has sped up the middle steps—so why is the whole team still waiting?

Tong Xi, CTO of P&G Greater China, shared their exploration: using Agents to connect R&D stages, getting tech colleagues involved in the business earlier, and then validating solutions with prototypes.

AI has sped up the middle steps—so why is the whole team still waiting?

Tong Xi, CTO of P&G Greater China, shared their exploration: using Agents to connect R&D stages, getting tech colleagues involved in the business earlier, and then validating solutions with prototypes.

Word count: 3,727
Reading time: about 12 minutes

P&G China is rebuilding its R&D process around ADLC (AI-driven software lifecycle), using Agents to connect the full chain from requirements to operations, forcing changes in organizational process and division of labor.

ADLC is essentially about replacing traditional role-based collaboration with agents, not just accelerating individual development tasks; the bottleneck shifts from "who does it" to "who decides"; the experience of a century-old company shows that the core of AI adoption lies in process redesign, not stacking up tools.

Intended for tech leads, DevOps engineers, and digital transformation architects.

Once an Agent can complete several stages in a row, companies have to answer three questions anew: how the process should flow, how the team should divide the work, and which judgments still need to be left to people.

At P&G China today, AI runs through the entire business chain: from consumer research, product R&D, brand marketing, and supply chain to customer service and more—AI has a foothold in every link.

en.title: Upgrading and Reshaping Enterprise AI-Native R&D Workflows
en.summary: Compiled from the August talk "Upgrading and Reshaping Enterprise AI Native R&D Workflows" by Song Wenlong (Wen Ke), senior technical expert at Alibaba Qoder, at AICon 2026 Shenzhen. Drawing on his own team's practice of using Coding Agent to build Coding Agent, along with rollout experience from multiple enterprise customers, he systematically examined the key problems Coding Agent must solve to move from an individual tool to a team-level production system. Covering SPEC-first, team-level Harness, Agent team and organizational transformation, he laid out a complete path from wish-driven programming to the on the loop R&D paradigm, and shared first-hand cases from Gaode, Shangou and inside Qoder.

一个并不AI原生的小团队，照常用微信和Notion，怎样接住一场千人大会前前后后几十轮修改？AIE上海我做的不只是后台，还有排议程、请嘉宾、宣传卖票和联系社区；这篇只复盘后台这一段：我人在西雅图，带着一个agent负责官网、议程和物料。从10月22日官网上线到大会结束，官网发布44次，73条修改需求上线66条，交付322张海报和大屏图。​
AI native不是每个环节都用上AI，而是保留大家最顺手的工作方式，找到其中最卡的那个限制，用AI把它撑大。 这次最卡的是交接：一条修改要在官网、PDF、海报、大屏之间传好几手。我们把这一整段交给一个人加一个agent走完。​
工具不换，只定一个“算数”的地方。 微信里商量，Notion里定稿

en.title: Behind the Scenes at AIE Shanghai: 50+ Speakers, a 1,000-Person Conference—How a Small Team Used AI to Seamlessly Absorb Dozens of Rounds of Changes
en.summary:
Behind the scenes at AIE Shanghai: 50+ speakers, a 1,000-person conference, and how a small team used AI invisibly to handle dozens of rounds of changes - Feishu Docs

Superlinear Academy

📌 This article is a repost; copyright belongs to the original author, and the full text is subject to the original link.

How does a team that isn't AI-native — still using WeChat and Notion as usual — absorb dozens of rounds of revisions before and after a 1,000-person conference? At AIE Shanghai I didn't just run the back office; I also built the agenda, invited speakers, handled promotion and ticket sales, and coordinated with communities. This piece recaps only the back-office part: I was in Seattle with a single agent responsible for the website, agenda and materials. From the site going live on October 22 to the end of the conference, the website shipped 44 releases, 66 of 73 change requests went live, and we delivered 322 posters and big-screen graphics.

Being AI native isn't about using AI at every step — it's about keeping the way everyone works most comfortably, finding the tightest bottleneck in it, and using AI to widen that bottleneck. This time the bottleneck was handoffs: a single change had to pass through several hands across the website, PDF, posters and the big screen. We handed that entire stretch to one person plus one agent to carry through.

Don't change tools, just designate one place that "counts." Discuss in WeChat, finalize in Notion

At the Claude Code team, the vast majority of our code (about 90%) is written by Claude and reviewed by Claude. At this scale, how we equip agents to verify their work with evidence becomes extremely important.

Verification loops are the cornerstone that lets you delegate more work to Claude. This weekend, Lao Jin was scrolling Hongguo when he came across a War of Resistance storyline that left him in tears.

Having made games for so long, a thought popped into my head as I watched: what if I put that feeling into an interactive AVG and let people play it themselves?

The AVG I wanted to make is that kind of story-driven adventure game. The story plays out in front of you, you can make choices, and you can also step in and lend a hand.

GPT's available capabilities this time didn't include video generation, so the game uses only images. It generated the images itself, found the voiceover model itself, searched the web for sound effects itself, and handled all the other effects itself too.

Caijing, citing QuestMobile data, reports that in July and August 2026, the Hongguo app averaged about 151 minutes of daily per-user time, versus 133.5 minutes for Douyin over the same period.

Spending that much time a day watching short dramas — what exactly are people watching?

Speaking for myself, when I watch short dramas, I like the face-slapping and contrast-driven plots.

Emotion keeps people there; only then does time have a chance to turn into business.

en.title: From SDLC to ADLC: P&G's AI-Native Organization Experiment
en.summary:
AI has sped up the middle steps—so why is the whole team still waiting?

Tong Xi, CTO of P&G Greater China, shared their exploration: using Agents to connect R&D stages, getting tech colleagues involved in the business earlier, and then validating solutions with prototypes.

AI has sped up the middle steps—so why is the whole team still waiting?

Tong Xi, CTO of P&G Greater China, shared their exploration: using Agents to connect R&D stages, getting tech colleagues involved in the business earlier, and then validating solutions with prototypes.

Word count: 3,727
Reading time: about 12 minutes

P&G China is rebuilding its R&D process around ADLC (AI-driven software lifecycle), using Agents to connect the full chain from requirements to operations, forcing changes in organizational process and division of labor.

ADLC is essentially about replacing traditional role-based collaboration with agents, not just accelerating individual development tasks; the bottleneck shifts from "who does it" to "who decides"; the experience of a century-old company shows that the core of AI adoption lies in process redesign, not stacking up tools.

Intended for tech leads, DevOps engineers, and digital transformation architects.

Once an Agent can complete several stages in a row, companies have to answer three questions anew: how the process should flow, how the team should divide the work, and which judgments still need to be left to people.

At P&G China today, AI runs through the entire business chain: from consumer research, product R&D, brand marketing, and supply chain to customer service and more—AI has a foothold in every link.

en.title: Upgrading and Reshaping Enterprise AI-Native R&D Workflows
en.summary: Compiled from the August talk "Upgrading and Reshaping Enterprise AI Native R&D Workflows" by Song Wenlong (Wen Ke), senior technical expert at Alibaba Qoder, at AICon 2026 Shenzhen. Drawing on his own team's practice of using Coding Agent to build Coding Agent, along with rollout experience from multiple enterprise customers, he systematically examined the key problems Coding Agent must solve to move from an individual tool to a team-level production system.
